title: Sociocultural approach: culture and behaviour
summary: Cultural dimensions, enculturation, acculturation, and emic and etic ways of studying culture.

keyterms.definition: Shared values, beliefs, norms and practices transmitted between generations in a group.
Hofstede's measurable ways in which national cultures differ, such as individualism–collectivism.
A cultural orientation emphasising personal goals, independence and individual achievement.
A cultural orientation emphasising group goals, interdependence and loyalty.
How far less powerful members of a society accept that power is distributed unequally.
Learning the norms and values of one's own culture, e.g. through family and school.
Psychological and cultural change when people from different cultures come into contact.
Stress caused by the challenges of adapting to a new culture.
Unwritten rules about expected behaviour in a group or culture.

questions.prompt: Hofstede's original cultural dimensions came from surveys of:
questions.explanation: Using one company controlled some variables but may not represent whole national populations.

questions.prompt: Which dimension describes acceptance of unequal power?
questions.explanation: High power distance cultures accept hierarchy more readily.

questions.statement: Cultural dimensions describe national averages and may not apply to every individual in a country.
questions.explanation: Applying them to individuals risks stereotyping; there is variation within cultures.

questions.statement: Enculturation refers to adapting to a new culture after migration.
questions.explanation: That is acculturation; enculturation is learning one's own culture.

questions.text: A culture that values group harmony and loyalty over personal goals is ___.
questions.explanation: Collectivism is the opposite pole of individualism on Hofstede's dimension.

questions.text: Unwritten rules for how to behave in a culture are called ___.
questions.explanation: Norms are transmitted through enculturation.

questions.prompt: Match each dimension to a description.
questions.explanation: Hofstede later added long-term orientation and indulgence to his original four.

questions.prompt: Bond and Smith (1996) linked higher conformity to collectivism. This illustrates:
questions.explanation: Collectivist values may make agreeing with the group more important.

questions.prompt: Which is a limitation of Hofstede's research?
options: Cultures change over time, but the data were originally collected decades ago
questions.explanation: Cultures change, so dimension scores may become outdated.

questions.prompt: Order how a norm is passed on through enculturation.
items: Child later passes the norm to their own children
questions.explanation: Enculturation involves social learning across generations.

questions.prompt: Berry (1997) proposed acculturation strategies. Keeping one's heritage culture while also adopting the new one is:
questions.explanation: Integration is usually linked to the best psychological outcomes.

questions.prompt: Rejecting the heritage culture and fully adopting the host culture is:
questions.explanation: Assimilation means giving up heritage culture for the host culture.

questions.statement: Marginalization, losing contact with both cultures, is linked to the highest acculturative stress.
questions.explanation: Berry's model links marginalization with poorest adaptation.

questions.statement: Acculturation only affects migrants, never the host culture.
questions.explanation: Acculturation is two-way: both groups may change, although usually unequally.

questions.text: Stress caused by adapting to a new culture is called ___ stress.
questions.explanation: It can involve language barriers, discrimination and loss of support.

questions.text: Berry's model is based on two questions: maintaining heritage culture, and seeking contact with the ___ culture.
questions.explanation: The answers to both questions give four strategies.

questions.prompt: Match Berry's strategies to their description.

pairs.right: Keep heritage and join host culture

questions.explanation: The four strategies come from crossing two yes/no dimensions.

questions.prompt: Lueck and Wilson (2010) studied acculturative stress in Asian immigrants to the USA. Which factor tended to reduce it?
options: Being bilingual and keeping ties to the heritage culture
questions.explanation: Bilingualism and family support were protective, consistent with integration benefits.

questions.prompt: A researcher uses a questionnaire developed in the USA to measure acculturation in Japanese migrants. The main risk is:
options: The measure may not capture culturally meaningful experiences (an etic imposition)
questions.explanation: Measures may not translate in meaning; emic methods can help.

questions.prompt: Order a typical acculturation process for a new migrant.
items: Arrival and first contact with the host culture
Experience of differences and possible stress
questions.explanation: Adaptation usually takes time and depends on the strategy and context.
